newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks swing higher in flimsy trade.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks swing higher in flimsy trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed 2.19 percent higher on Wednesday in in volatile, thin trade helped by gains in other markets, dealers said.
They did not see the market settling down in the short term and expected the seesaw movements to continue for several weeks.
The general index rose 12.9 points, 2.19 percent, to 602.71 and the Ibex-35 gained 171.24 points, 2.56 percent, to 6,868.32.
Endesa surged up five percent, 160 pesetas, to 3,300 outperforming the market after better than expected first half results.

The utility said first half net profit had fallen 3.9 percent to 78.59 billion pesetas, but dealers said the market was satisfied the drop in earnings was a one-off restatement of assets and results had actually improved from the first quarter.
"The underlying results were not out of line, in fact they were better than expected," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market swing was exacerbated by small trading volume of 62.7 billion pesetas, much less than a month earlier. They said there was a wide range of movement upcoming.
"It seems there's room to climb in the Ibex to 7,200 points without problems and the floor is around 6,650," a dealer said.
